title: R3 post-draw glow dies one frame after the commit lands — glow_gen stores the pre-apply generation
detail: The commit path captures `app.glow_gen = app.state.topology.gen` at commit time, but the draw is only QUEUED (`apply_tick = app.tick + 1`) — the live topology's gen is still the pre-apply value and bumps on the next step. The render gate requires `app.state.topology.gen == app.glow_gen`, so the committed R3 glow renders for exactly one frame (the commit frame) and dies the moment the edit lands — not for glow_ticks (120) as the R3 acceptance criterion requires. The code's own comment ('glow_gen is the POST-apply gen (== the clone's gen)') and preview_compute's header ('the clone's gen == the live gen + 1 ... apply bumps once') confirm the intended stored value is live gen + 1.
suggestion: Store the post-apply generation: `app.glow_gen = app.state.topology.gen + 1` (or expose the scratch clone's post-apply gen and store that). Add an assertion/test that the glow survives past the apply tick.

title: S5 passes but does not test its stated premise — the on_edge/heading start is unpinned and the comment references a different topology than the one built
detail: S5 claims to pin the mid-flight rule ('a packet on an edge re-decides at its heading node (E29); a candidate that only helps upstream must not fire'), but the candidate {1,3,wide} attaches AT the packet's next junction (node 1), not upstream of it — and node 3 has no onward pipe (S5 pre-draws only 0-1, 1-2, 2-4; unlike S3 it does NOT pre-draw 3-4). The candidate is therefore a dead end for every packet position, so preview_compute returns false regardless of whether it starts at `at_node` or `heading`. The assertion would still pass if the heading-node logic were deleted entirely — a regression in the E29 handling is not caught. The comment's 'the same topology with the packet at the junction does fire (S3 covers the junction case)' is also inaccurate: S3's topology differs (it pre-draws 3-4 std), which is exactly what turns the candidate into a tie there.
suggestion: Rebuild S5 so the outcome depends on the heading-node start: use a candidate the packet has already passed (e.g. a second pipe on the 0-1 pair) and assert no preview fires mid-edge, plus a counter-case where the same candidate DOES fire when the packet is still at the source node (not yet forwarded). As written, the scenario must fail if the on_edge/heading logic breaks.

title: tools/harness.sh is never modified — the new CI gate depends on unverified script pass-through
detail: The diff adds the `tools/harness.sh preview-check` CI step and the harness binary's `preview-check` verb, but never touches `tools/harness.sh`. If the script whitelists verbs, builds the harness with fixed args, or otherwise does not forward `preview-check` (and does not build the render package with the now-required #load embed of data/assist.json), the new CI gate breaks. Nothing in the diff proves the pass-through.
suggestion: Verify `tools/harness.sh` forwards the verb verbatim to `odin run harness -- <verb>` (like drift-check) and that the harness build resolves the `#load("../../data/assist.json")` embed; add the script change to the diff if one is needed.

title: topology_clone_into hand-copies an explicit field list — completeness unverifiable; a missing field silently diverges the preview from the sim
detail: The what-if clone copies 15 arrays plus next_node_id/next_pipe_id/gen by name. The full Topology struct definition is not in the diff, so completeness cannot be verified. Any field omitted today (or added to Topology later without updating this list) is silently zero/stale in the clone — routing_rebuild would then price the what-if table differently from the post-commit rebuild, which is precisely the divergence the preview-check gate exists to prevent. The seven scenarios only exercise the fields they happen to touch, so a stale field outside their paths would ship green.
suggestion: Move the clone into core as a topology_copy/clone kept next to the struct (so new fields cannot be forgotten), or add a reflection/compile-time assertion that every Topology field is covered; at minimum, add a scenario exercising each field routing_rebuild reads.

title: draws_since_nudge counts every commit, not 'N successful draws in Full mode'
detail: `app.draws_since_nudge += 1` runs on every successful commit regardless of assist mode and regardless of whether the preview fired (dead-end draws and parallel-pipe no-ops increment it too). A player who spends most draws in Glow_Only/Off and later switches to Full triggers the nudge after fewer than N Full-mode draws — diverging from the spec's 'N successful draws, mode Full' trigger. (A T press latches nudge_done, which usually masks this, but the counter semantics still diverge.)
suggestion: Only increment when `assist_mode == .Full` (and arguably only when the preview fired), or document the all-mode counting as intended.

title: A commit with no live preview extinguishes a still-running R3 glow and leaves a stale glow buffer
detail: In the commit path, `else { app.glow_until = 0 }` kills a previous commit's R3 glow mid-window when the new commit had no preview (dead-end draw, parallel-pipe no-op). The spec's R3 criterion says the winning path 'keeps glowing for glow_ticks' — a subsequent no-op draw truncates that. Additionally the glow buffer is not released/cleared in that branch, so a stale DAG (glow.ok still true) remains, guarded only by the tick gate.
suggestion: Only reset glow_until when the new commit produces a glow that should replace the old one, and call preview_clear/preview_release on the glow buffer when deliberately killing it.

title: Any active drag blanks the committed R3 glow, even drags with no valid candidate
detail: The render gate draws the live preview only when `preview_live && preview.ok`, and the committed glow only when `!app.drag.active`. Starting a drag with an invalid or unsnapped candidate therefore hides the R3 glow for the entire drag (flicker), even though nothing new is being previewed. Minor, but visible when a player starts a sloppy drag during the glow window.
suggestion: Fall back to the committed glow when a drag is active but preview_live is false, or keep the glow visible until the first valid preview appears.

title: Cross-check hash-pick inputs (ecmp_pick) must exactly match the sim's forward-time pick
detail: packet_path_matches verifies the packet's 'actual path' with `pp.ecmp_pick(p.src, p.dst, u8(p.class), p.id, count)`. If the sim's forwarding decision keys the pick on different inputs (e.g., the current junction node or the tick) or evaluates it at a different node than the walker assumes, the cross-check validates a different function than the sim actually runs — the tie scenario (S3) would pass while the real game diverges. The diff cannot prove the call matches the flow's pick exactly.
suggestion: Verify ecmp_pick's signature and the flow's call site match (same inputs, same evaluation node); ideally export the flow's own pick wrapper and call that from the check.
